cells.tense: Fresh sight is arriving now, and you are meeting it with the pen still down.
cells.act: stay in the depth of it instead of surfacing
cells.ask: Notice something this week and follow it well past the point where it gets comfortable. Sit in that thread twenty minutes longer than you normally would.
cells.core:
A way of seeing is opening that hasn't cut anything yet. Something is being looked at cleanly for the first time, before it has a label, and you're in it early. Most people grab a name the moment it shows up. You don't have to. The fresh look is the part that's working.

What keeps this alive is depth. Follow a thread past where it gets comfortable instead of surfacing for air. Your mind goes down into a subject until it meets the floor of it, and that isn't a problem to manage here. Sit with that thread twenty minutes longer than usual. The understanding that comes when you stay is what this beginning is for.
cells.sheetLine: Let the new look deepen before you name it.
cells.verb: seeing something for the first time, before it has a name
cells.place: the doorway where what is outside arrives and gets met

cells.tense: The first clear look arrives and you are already turning future pages inside it.
cells.act: complete what you began by beginning it
cells.ask: Put whatever you've glimpsed in the world as a finished thing — the note written, the call made, the purchase done — then stop, before you run ahead into the next step in your head.
cells.core:
Clear sight is sharp and it wants to be everywhere at once. Something new shows up and you're building the whole future on it, adding rooms before you've stood in the first one. What's arriving is only a beginning; the strain is that you treat it like a finished blueprint when the edges haven't even appeared. Your gift for pattern gets spent on what hasn't happened instead of what just showed up.

Finish the look by putting it in the world. Write the note, make the call, complete the purchase — a finished thing, not a plan — then stop there. The doing closes the loop. When the first piece holds, the next arrival comes when it's ready instead of being hauled in ahead of schedule by you.

cells.tense: A new seeing waits at the door, and you have not turned from the last stretch.
cells.act: bring the directed work to its full standing
cells.ask: Close out a piece of work you already started — send the file, shelve the object, make the last call — and then look up at whatever is waiting.
cells.core:
Something is trying to arrive and you're still looking back at what already happened, replaying how it went. New sight is here and you haven't turned toward it. The equipment works fine; your face is turned toward the previous stretch, and what's trying to come in is waiting for someone to meet it.

Finish a piece of work you already directed, and finish it in the smallest complete way so nothing keeps pulling your attention back. Send the file, shelve the object, make the last call. Then your face is free to turn. What's arriving has somewhere to land once you look.
cells.sheetLine: You're listening to the last stretch while the next one waits.

cells.tense: Fresh entry is arriving by your own hand, and you describe it as something you happened to notice.
cells.act: let this moment be a fresh entry, not a continuation
cells.ask: At the start of something routine — the same walk, the same meeting — take a slow breath and treat it as an arrival rather than a repeat. Do it again next time.
cells.core:
The perceiving is yours. What comes in comes through your attention, fresh each time, and your version has it arriving by itself while you happen to be nearby. You talk as though the sight was already out there and you were lucky enough to walk past it. The turn is being made. Nobody watching from outside can tell, so nobody corrects you.

At the start of something routine — the same walk, the same meeting — take a slow breath and treat it as an arrival rather than a repeat. You'll feel the shift right away, which is how you know the door was yours to open. Do it again next time, and make that the whole of the practice.
cells.sheetLine: You're the door, and you think you merely walked through.
